# Are your lien deadlines still open?

> Free calculator for the preliminary notice and lien filing deadlines a subcontractor or supplier faces in California, Texas, Florida, Arizona, Washington, Georgia, Colorado, North Carolina, New York, Ohio, Michigan, Minnesota, Nevada, Oregon, Utah and Virginia. Enter your first and last day on the job; see both dates, weekend flags, and days left. Entirely client-side, nothing uploaded.

Free to use and source available (FSL-1.1-MIT). Results are estimates from the numbers typed in, not legal, tax, financial or professional advice.

## What it covers

- Texas: one notice date per month of unpaid work (15th day of the 3rd month after it, 2nd on residential), lien affidavit 15th of the 4th (3rd) month; rules for original contracts from 2022-01-01, the same for every tier.
- Georgia: Notice to Contractor shown only for second-tier claimants (hired by a subcontractor), as the statute requires it only without privity with the contractor.
- Washington: a subcontractor hired by the prime contractor owes no notice of right to claim a lien (RCW 60.04.031(2)(c)), except on repair or remodel of an existing owner-occupied single-family home; second-tier claimants get the 60-day (10-day on a new single-family home) look-back.
- Late notices: California and Arizona protect work from 20 days before a late notice, Washington 60 (10); Florida treats a late Notice to Owner as a complete defense to the lien (713.06(2)(a)). A passed date shows the earliest work a notice served today still covers.
- Each result links the statute sections it uses; timing checked against the statute text on 2026-11-25 (California's sub lien clock is Civ. Code § 8414).
- California, Arizona, Florida, Colorado, North Carolina, New York: the same clocks for first- and second-tier claimants.
- North Carolina: Notice to Lien Agent 15 days after first furnishing (projects with a designated lien agent); claim of lien 120 days after last furnishing (G.S. 44A-11.2, 44A-12).
- New York: no preliminary notice on private work; notice of lien 8 months after final furnishing, 4 months on a single family dwelling (Lien Law § 10).
- Ohio: notice of furnishing 21 days after first furnishing where a notice of commencement was recorded; affidavit of lien 75 days after last furnishing, 60 on a one- or two-family dwelling (R.C. 1311.05, 1311.06).
- Michigan: notice of furnishing 20 days after first furnishing (MCL 570.1109(1)); claim of lien 90 days after last furnishing (MCL 570.1111(1)).
- Minnesota (§ 514.08, 120 days after last furnishing), Nevada (NRS 108.226, 90 days after the later of completion and last furnishing, 40 after a notice of completion), Oregon (ORS 87.035, 75 days after last furnishing or completion, whichever is earlier), Utah (§ 38-1a-502, 180 days after final completion, 90 after a notice of completion), Virginia (§ 43-4, 90 days from the end of the month of last furnishing, no later than 90 after completion): the lien filing only; their earlier notices are not dated.
- Delaware (25 Del. C. § 2711(b), 120 days after last furnishing, subs), Idaho (§ 45-507, 90 days), Kansas (K.S.A. 60-1103, 3 months, subs; 4 months for a contractor with the owner), Maryland (Real Prop. §§ 9-104, 9-105, notice of intention 120 days, petition 180 days), Montana (MCA 71-3-535, 90 days, or after a notice of completion), Nebraska (§ 52-137, 120 days), North Dakota (N.D.C.C. 35-27-13, 90 days), South Carolina (§ 29-5-90, 90 days) and South Dakota (SDCL 44-9-15, 120 days): lien filing only, added 2026-11-28 from each state's own code site.
- Alabama (Ala. Code § 35-11-215, 4 months after last furnishing, subs; 6 months for an original contractor), Alaska (AS 34.35.068, 120 days, or 15 days after a recorded notice of completion for some claimants), Maine (10 M.R.S. § 3255, court action within 120 days), Rhode Island (R.I. Gen. Laws § 34-28-4, notice of intention mailed and filed within 200 days) and Wyoming (W.S. 29-2-106, 120 days after the earlier of last furnishing and substantial completion; notice of intention 20 days before, 29-2-107): added 2026-11-28 (second batch) from each state's own code site.
- The same thirty states' lien dates are kept on every job in PayApps, hosted pay-app billing: [start free](https://payapps.marisstella.app/?signup&from=mechanics-lien-deadline-calculator).
- Related: [pay application guides](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/) (schedule of values, retainage, lien waivers).

## Answers

The questions each page answers in its "Common questions" section, with the answer as the page states it. Each link opens that section; the page has the sources.

- [What is a preliminary notice in a mechanics lien claim?](https://marisstella.app/mechanics-lien-deadline-calculator/#faq): A preliminary notice (called a Notice to Owner in Florida, a notice of claim for unpaid labor or materials in Texas, and a 20-day preliminary notice in Arizona) is a written notice a subcontractor or supplier sends to the owner and general contractor early in a job, to preserve the right to file a lien later. Several states make it a condition of lien rights, so a missed deadline can cost the claim.
- [How long do I have to file a mechanics lien after finishing the work?](https://marisstella.app/mechanics-lien-deadline-calculator/#faq): It depends on the state. California allows 90 days after completion of the project, or 30 days after the owner records a notice of completion. Florida allows 90 days after your last furnishing, Washington 90 days after your last furnishing, Arizona 120 days after completion or 60 days after a recorded notice of completion, and Texas the 15th day of the 4th month on commercial work or the 3rd month on residential work.
- [When does the preliminary notice clock start?](https://marisstella.app/mechanics-lien-deadline-calculator/#faq): For California, Arizona, Florida, and Washington it starts on the day you first furnished labor or materials: 20 days in California and Arizona, 45 days in Florida, and 60 days in Washington (10 days on new single-family residential work). Texas instead counts months: the 15th day of the 3rd month after the month of unpaid work on commercial jobs, or the 2nd month on residential jobs.
- [Do I need a separate Texas notice for every month of work?](https://marisstella.app/mechanics-lien-deadline-calculator/#faq): Yes. On Texas contracts signed from 2022, each month of unpaid labor or materials has its own notice date: the 15th day of the 3rd month after that month on commercial work, or the 2nd month on residential work. The calculator lists one date per month from your first to your last day on the job.
- [Does it matter whether the general contractor or a subcontractor hired me?](https://marisstella.app/mechanics-lien-deadline-calculator/#faq): Among the thirty states here it changes the result in Georgia and Washington. Georgia requires a Notice to Contractor only from claimants without a direct contract with the general contractor. Washington exempts a subcontractor hired by the prime contractor from its notice, except on repair or remodel of an existing owner-occupied single-family home (RCW 60.04.031(2)(c), (3)(b)). Texas gives every tier the same notice dates on contracts from 2022; earlier Texas projects had an extra 2nd-month notice for second-tier claimants.
- [Do North Carolina, New York and Ohio need a preliminary notice?](https://marisstella.app/mechanics-lien-deadline-calculator/#faq): North Carolina asks for a Notice to Lien Agent within 15 days of first furnishing on projects with a designated lien agent, and the claim of lien is due 120 days after your last furnishing. New York has no preliminary notice on private work; the notice of lien is due 8 months after your final work or materials, or 4 months on a single family dwelling. Ohio asks a subcontractor or supplier for a notice of furnishing within 21 days of first furnishing where a notice of commencement was recorded, and the affidavit of lien is due 75 days after your last furnishing, or 60 days on a one- or two-family home.
- [What are the lien deadlines in Michigan, Minnesota, Nevada, Oregon, Utah and Virginia?](https://marisstella.app/mechanics-lien-deadline-calculator/#faq): Michigan: record the claim of lien within 90 days after your last furnishing (MCL 570.1111(1)), after a notice of furnishing within 20 days of first furnishing (MCL 570.1109(1)). Minnesota: file the lien statement and serve a copy on the owner within 120 days after your last furnishing (Minn. Stat. § 514.08). Nevada: record the notice of lien within 90 days after the later of completion and your own last furnishing, or 40 days after a recorded notice of completion (NRS 108.226). Oregon: 75 days after your last furnishing or after completion of construction, whichever is earlier (ORS 87.035). Utah: 180 days after final completion of the original contract, or 90 days after a notice of completion (Utah Code § 38-1a-502). Virginia: 90 days from the last day of the month you last furnished, and no later than 90 days after the building is completed (Va. Code § 43-4).
- [What are the lien deadlines in Delaware, Idaho, Kansas, Maryland, Montana, Nebraska, North Dakota, South Carolina and South Dakota?](https://marisstella.app/mechanics-lien-deadline-calculator/#faq): For a subcontractor or supplier: Delaware, file the statement of claim within 120 days after your last labor or delivery (25 Del. C. § 2711(b)). Idaho, file the claim of lien within 90 days after you last furnished (Idaho Code § 45-507). Kansas, file the lien statement within 3 months after your last furnishing, 4 months for a contractor with the owner (K.S.A. 60-1103, 60-1102). Maryland, give the owner notice of intention to claim a lien within 120 days and file the petition in circuit court within 180 days after the work or materials (Real Prop. §§ 9-104, 9-105). Montana, file the lien within 90 days after your final furnishing, or after the owner files a notice of completion (MCA 71-3-535). Nebraska, record the lien within 120 days after your final furnishing (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 52-137). North Dakota, record the lien within 90 days after your contribution is done (N.D.C.C. 35-27-13). South Carolina, serve the owner and file the statement of account within 90 days after you stop furnishing (S.C. Code § 29-5-90). South Dakota, file the statement of the claim within 120 days after your last work or materials (SDCL 44-9-15).
- [What are the lien deadlines in Alabama, Alaska, Maine, Rhode Island and Wyoming?](https://marisstella.app/mechanics-lien-deadline-calculator/#faq): For a subcontractor or supplier: Alabama, file the verified statement with the judge of probate within 4 months after your last work or material, after written notice to the owner; an original contractor has 6 months (Ala. Code §§ 35-11-215, 35-11-218). Alaska, record the claim of lien within 120 days after you complete your contract or stop furnishing, or within 15 days after the owner records a notice of completion if you gave no notice of right to lien (AS 34.35.068). Maine, file the action to enforce the lien in court within 120 days after your last labor, materials or services (10 M.R.S. § 3255). Rhode Island, mail the notice of intention to the owner and file a copy in the land evidence records within 200 days after the work; it covers only work in the 200 days before filing (R.I. Gen. Laws § 34-28-4). Wyoming, file the lien statement within 120 days after the earlier of your last day of work and substantial completion of the project, after a notice of intention at least 20 days before (W.S. 29-2-106, 29-2-107); a contractor with the owner has 150 days.
- [What happens if I send the preliminary notice late?](https://marisstella.app/mechanics-lien-deadline-calculator/#faq): It depends on the state. In California and Arizona a late notice still counts but protects only work furnished in the 20 days before it was given, and everything after (Cal. Civ. Code § 8204, Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-992.01). Washington works the same way with 60 days, or 10 days on a new single-family home (RCW 60.04.031). In Florida a missing or late Notice to Owner is a complete defense to the lien (Fla. Stat. § 713.06(2)(a)). When the date has passed, the calculator gives the earliest work date a notice served today still covers.
- [Why does the calculator use my last furnishing date when I do not know the completion date?](https://marisstella.app/mechanics-lien-deadline-calculator/#faq): Some states measure the lien deadline from completion of the whole project. Your own last day on the job can only be the same as or earlier than completion, so using it gives the same date or an earlier, safer one. In California, Arizona, Nevada and Utah entering the real completion date can only move the deadline later. Oregon and Virginia take whichever comes first, your last furnishing or completion, so if the building was completed before your last day of work, entering that date moves the deadline earlier.
- [Is this legal advice?](https://marisstella.app/mechanics-lien-deadline-calculator/#faq): No. This tool applies a simplified reading of published state timing rules to the dates you enter, for a subcontractor or supplier hired by the general contractor or by a subcontractor. It does not model third-tier claimants, public projects, required notice content, delivery method, or foreclosure deadlines, and lien rights can be lost by missing a deadline. Confirm every date with a construction attorney or the current statute before relying on it.
